mainTopic: A שליח who changes his instructions, whether a seller must know about the sender, and buying a field in someone else's name
overview: Someone gave money to a שליח to buy wheat, and the שליח bought barley instead (or the reverse). Two ברייתות disagree about who gets the profit, though both put any loss on the שליח. רבי יוחנן says one ברייתא follows רבי מאיר (שינוי קונה) and the other follows רבי יהודה (שינוי אינו קונה). רבי אלעזר disagrees and says both follow רבי מאיר: one is about grain bought to eat, the other about grain bought to sell. The scholars of ארץ ישראל mock רבי יוחנן's version of רבי יהודה, since the seller never knew about the sender. רבי אבהו explains that a שליח who keeps his mission counts as the sender himself, and he tries to prove it from a משנה in ערכין about a wife's clothes. רבי אבא rejects that proof and, after challenges from רבי זירא and רב אושעיא, settles on a new reason: the family's clothes count as already given to them. Finally the גמרא brings a ברייתא about buying a field in someone else's name. רב ששת's reading, using the name of the ריש גלותא, is rejected, and אביי begins a new reading that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree about an agent who bought the wrong grain
steps.stepSummary: A שליח was sent to buy wheat but bought barley, or the reverse. One ברייתא gives all the profit to the שליח. Another ברייתא splits the profit. This is a contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone gave money to buy wheat and the agent bought barley, or gave money for barley and he bought wheat: One ברייתא teaches that if there was a loss, it is his, and if there was a profit, it is his. Another ברייתא teaches that if there was a loss, it is his, but if there was a profit, it is split down the middle!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts two ברייתות side by side that seem to contradict each other about the same case. This sets up the question that the rest of the section will try to answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות agree that a loss falls on the שליח, because he did not follow instructions. They disagree only about profit. The first gives it all to the שליח, as if the deal became his own. The second says the profit is shared, as if the deal still belongs to both of them.

keyTerms.meaning: An agent sent to do something on someone else's behalf
It was taught in one ברייתא... and it was taught in another (the formula for showing a contradiction)
There was a loss (literally, 'they decreased')
There was a profit (literally, 'they increased')
To the middle, meaning split between both parties

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתות argue about the loss. Both agree the loss is on the שליח. The only argument is about who gets the profit.

phrases.english: [If he gave money to his agent] to buy wheat for him,
and he bought barley with it;
[or to buy] barley, and he bought wheat with it:
It is taught in one [ברייתא]:
if there was a loss, the loss is his,
and if there was a profit, the profit is his;
and it is taught in another [ברייתא]:
if there was a loss, the loss is his,
and if there was a profit, the profit goes to the middle!

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא חֲדָא אִם פָּחֲתוּ פָּחֲתוּ לוֹ וְאִם הוֹתִירוּ הוֹתִירוּ לוֹ וְתָנֵי חֲדָא
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about the agent who bought a different grain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same case gets two different rulings about the profit: all to the agent, or split.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: each ברייתא follows a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers the contradiction. The first ברייתא follows רבי מאיר and the second follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It is not difficult. This one follows רבי מאיר, and this one follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן solves the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות simply follow two different תנאים who disagree. He will explain the reason in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of saying the cases are different, רבי יוחנן says the ברייתות reflect an existing מחלוקת. This kind of answer, 'this one is like X and that one is like Y,' is very common in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
This one... and that one

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: this is [the view of] Rabbi Meir, and this is [the view of] Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns each source to a different תנא (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed both ברייתות were one consistent opinion that contradicted itself
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתות follow רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה respectively

steps.title: The reason: שינוי קונה versus שינוי אינו קונה
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that a change makes the item the agent's, so he gets all the profit. רבי יהודה holds that a change does not, so the profit is shared.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא is רבי מאיר, who says a change acquires. That ברייתא is רבי יהודה, who says a change does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each ברייתא matches each תנא. It is about whether going against instructions makes the item belong to the agent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, once the שליח changed the instructions, the grain became his own, so all profit goes to him. According to רבי יהודה, the grain still belongs to the partnership, so the profit is split. In both views the שליח pays for any loss, because he caused it by changing the instructions. This is the same מחלוקת the משנה brought earlier about a dyer who used a different color than he was told.

keyTerms.meaning: A change; here, going against the owner's instructions
A change acquires: the one who made the change now owns the item
A change does not acquire: the item stays with the original owner

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר says שינוי קונה, so all profit goes to the שליח. רבי יהודה says שינוי אינו קונה, so the profit is split. Both put the loss on the שליח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links a business case about agents to the well-known מחלוקת about שינוי, and that link is exactly what רבי אלעזר will question next.

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, דְּאָמַר שִׁינּוּי קוֹנֶה;
phrases.english: This is Rabbi Meir, who says a change acquires;
phrases.notes: "A change acquires" means that by not following the instructions, the agent now owns the item himself.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר שִׁינּוּי אֵינוֹ קוֹנֶה.
phrases.english: and this is Rabbi Yehuda, who says a change does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר שִׁינּוּי קוֹנֶה וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּאָמַר שִׁינּוּי אֵינוֹ קוֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's answer in step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Grounds the split in the מחלוקת about שינוי
steps.terutzMaskana: First ברייתא follows שינוי קונה (רבי מאיר); second follows שינוי אינו קונה (רבי יהודה)

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: maybe רבי מאיר's rule does not apply to goods bought for resale
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר challenges רבי יוחנן. How do we know רבי מאיר's rule reaches this case? Maybe he only said שינוי קונה about things used personally, not about merchandise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר objected: How do you know? Maybe רבי מאיר only said his rule about something the owner needed for his own use. But about merchandise bought to resell, he did not say it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר attacks רבי יוחנן's answer. He argues that רבי מאיר's rule might be too narrow to explain the first ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an item is for personal use, a change can ruin it for the owner, like wool dyed the wrong color. That is why the agent might be made to keep it. But with merchandise, the owner only wants profit, so barley or wheat may make little difference to him. So even רבי מאיר might say the deal stays with the owner. If so, the first ברייתא no longer fits רבי מאיר, and the contradiction comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it; a strong challenge to a statement
From where [do you know this]?
Perhaps
He only said his ruling up to here, meaning in this case only
For business, as merchandise to sell

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is not saying רבי מאיר disagrees with שינוי קונה. He is saying that rule may only cover personal-use items, so it may not explain this case of merchandise.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar objected to it:
From where [do you know this]?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר –
phrases.english: Perhaps Rabbi Meir only said [his ruling]
about something that is fit for his own use,
phrases.notes: "His own use" means the owner wanted the item to use himself, not to sell.

phrases.english: but [about something bought] for business, he did not say [it]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in steps 2–3
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the first ברייתא follows רבי מאיר's שינוי קונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר's rule may be limited to personal-use items. With merchandise even he might keep the deal with the owner, so the first ברייתא is not explained.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's own answer: both ברייתות follow רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers the contradiction differently. Both ברייתות follow רבי מאיר. One is about grain for eating and the other is about grain for selling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אלעזר said: both ברייתות follow רבי מאיר, and there is no contradiction. One is talking about grain bought to eat, and the other is talking about grain bought to sell.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר just attacked רבי יוחנן's answer. Now he offers his own way to explain why the two ברייתות disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the ברייתות follow two different תנאים. רבי אלעזר says both follow one תנא, רבי מאיר, and they simply describe two different kinds of purchases. When the wheat was wanted for eating, barley is useless to the sender, so the change matters and the שליח keeps the profit. When it was bought as merchandise, the sender does not care which grain it is, so the deal stays partly his and the profit is split.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one: both sources
For eating (personal use)
For business (to sell)
And it is not difficult: there is no contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up which ברייתא is which. The case of grain for eating is the one where the שליח keeps all the profit. The case of grain for merchandise is the one where the profit is split.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Elazar said:
Both this one and that one are Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: "This one and that one" means the two ברייתות from Step 1.

phrases.english: and it is not difficult:
here, it is grain for eating,
there, it is grain for merchandise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הָא וְהָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי אלעזר's challenge in Step 4 by offering his own answer to the contradiction from Step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): one תנא, two different kinds of purchase
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות seemed to contradict each other, or seemed to need two different תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבי מאיר. The rule of שינוי applies to food for eating but not to merchandise.

steps.title: The scholars in ארץ ישראל laugh at רבי יוחנן's version of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they mocked רבי יוחנן's claim that according to רבי יהודה the sender gets the grain. The seller never knew about the sender, so how could he transfer it to him?
steps.simpleTranslation: They laughed at this in the West, at רבי יוחנן's explanation of רבי יהודה: who told the seller of the wheat that he should transfer the wheat to the man whose money it was?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a sharp attack from ארץ ישראל on רבי יוחנן's explanation of רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that according to רבי יהודה a change does not make the item the שליח's, so the sender owns part of it. The mockers ask how the sender could become the owner at all. The seller dealt only with the שליח and never meant to transfer anything to someone he did not know about.

keyTerms.meaning: They laughed at it: they mocked this idea
In the West: ארץ ישראל
The owner of the wheat: the seller
The owner of the money: the sender

phrases.english: They laughed at it in the West:
phrases.notes: "The West" is the usual name in the גמרא for ארץ ישראל, which is west of Bavel.

phrases.english: at Rabbi Yochanan's explanation according to Rabbi Yehuda:
And who informed the owner of the wheat
that he should transfer the wheat to the owner of the money?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי יוחנן's explanation from Steps 2 and 3 and attacks the רבי יהודה side of it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that according to רבי יהודה the sender shares in the barley the שליח bought
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The seller never knew about the sender, so he never meant to transfer the grain to him. The sender should not be able to acquire it.

steps.title: רב שמואל בר ססרטי pushes back: then no שליח could ever buy anything
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר ססרטי rejects the mockery. If that reasoning were right, even a שליח who bought exactly what he was told to buy could not get it for his sender.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר ססרטי objects: if so, then even when the שליח was sent for wheat and bought wheat, the sender should also not get it!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone defends רבי יוחנן by showing that the mockers' question proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a normal case of שליחות the seller also often does not know about the sender, yet everyone agrees the sender gets the item. So the seller's not knowing cannot be the problem. That knocks down the laughter from ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it
If so: if your reasoning were true
Wheat and wheat: sent for wheat and bought wheat (no change)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר סַסְרָטִי:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Sasrati objects to it:
If so,
even when sent for wheat and he bought wheat, the sender should also not acquire it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר סַסְרָטִי אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the mockery of Step 6 by showing it would wipe out all שליחות.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole argument from ארץ ישראל in Step 6
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It proves too much. It would mean a sender never acquires through a שליח, even with no change at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The argument from ארץ ישראל in step 6 that the sender cannot acquire because the seller never knew about him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the seller's not knowing blocked acquisition, then even a שליח sent for wheat who bought wheat could not acquire for his sender, which cannot be right.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: a שליח doing his job counts as the owner himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו defends the mockers' view. When the שליח buys what he was sent for, he is doing his mission, so he counts as the owner himself and the seller's knowledge does not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: wheat for wheat is different, because the שליח is carrying out his mission, and so he is like the owner himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers רב שמואל בר ססרטי. He explains why a normal שליח works even though a שליח who changed his mission does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the שליח does exactly what he was asked, he stands in the sender's place. It is as if the sender bought the grain himself, so the seller does not need to know about him. When the שליח changes his mission he is no longer acting as the sender, so the question from ארץ ישראל comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
He is doing his mission
He is like the owner himself

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key idea about שליחות: a שליח who sticks to his mission is treated as the sender himself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
Wheat for wheat is different,
since he is carrying out his mission,
and he is like the owner himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ שָׁאנֵי חִטִּין וְחִטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 7 and saves the point made in Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling the cases apart: a שליח who keeps his mission versus one who changes it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seller's not knowing about the sender would block even a normal שליח.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שליח who keeps his mission counts as the sender himself. Only after a change does the seller's knowledge matter.

steps.title: Proof from a משנה: items bought for wife and children are not taken by הקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו brings a משנה. When someone gives his property or his ערך to the Temple, the Temple does not take his wife's and children's clothes, or the dye and new sandals he bought for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that this is true, because we learned in a משנה: whether a man makes all his property הקדש or pledges his own ערך, the Temple has no claim on his wife's clothes, his children's clothes, dye he dyed for them, or new sandals he bought for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו backs up his idea with a proof from a משנה in ערכין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man paid for these items himself, yet because he bought them for his wife and children, they count as theirs and the Temple cannot take them. This supports the idea that a purchase made for someone else can belong to that person.

keyTerms.meaning: Know it: here is a proof
One who gives all his property to the Temple
One who pledges his own ערך (fixed value) to the Temple
Clothing
For them: on their behalf

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבהו's view: a שליח who does his job stands in the sender's place. The משנה in ערכין shows that things bought for someone else can count as that person's.

phrases.english: Know that this is so, for we learned in a mishna:
Both one who consecrates his property
and one who pledges his own value to the Temple:
it has no claim to his wife's clothing,
phrases.notes: "It" is the Temple treasury: it can't collect these items.

phrases.english: nor to his children's clothing,
nor to dyed clothing that he dyed for them,
nor to new sandals that he bought for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אבהו's rule from Step 8 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבהו's idea that something bought for another person can belong to that person
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in ערכין 24a about הקדש and ערכין: the wife's and children's clothes, dye and new sandals are not taken by the Temple

steps.title: The husband is like his wife's hand, so the agent is like the buyer's hand
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו finishes his proof. The dyer never knew he was giving dye to the wife, yet she owns it. That must be because the husband is doing her mission. The same applies to the שליח who buys grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does the wife own it? Let us ask here too: who told the dyer that he should transfer his dye to the wife? Rather, isn't it because we say that he is doing her mission and is like his wife's hand? Here too, the agent is doing his mission and is like the owner's hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו draws the lesson from the משנה he quoted in step 9. He shows that it supports his rule about a שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mockers asked how the seller could transfer grain to a sender he never knew about. רבי אבהו shows the same question would apply to the dyer and the wife. Since the wife clearly owns the dye, a person carrying out someone else's mission must count as that person's own hand.

keyTerms.meaning: He is doing his mission (acting as the agent)
Dyer
Like the hand of (an extension of the person)
The owner (here, the one who sent the agent)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core idea of רבי אבהו's answer. An agent who stays within his mission acts as the sender himself, so the seller does not need to know about the sender.

phrases.english: And why?
phrases.notes: Why does the Temple leave the clothes and dye for the wife and children, when the husband paid for them?

phrases.english: Let us say here too:
Who informed the dyer
that he should transfer his dye to the wife?
Rather, is it not because we say
that he is doing her mission,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording. They lay out the wife's case first, before applying it to the grain.

phrases.english: and he is like his wife's hand?
Here too,
he is doing his mission,
phrases.notes: Now he means the agent who bought the grain.

phrases.english: and he is like the owner's hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the משנה quoted in step 9 and applies it to the שליח case.
steps.raayaObject: A שליח who carries out his mission counts as the sender's own hand, even if the seller does not know about the sender.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about consecrated property: the wife owns the dye even though the dyer never knew about her.

steps.title: The real reason: he never meant to give his family's clothes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא rejects the proof. The clothes stay with the family because a man who gives his property to the Temple does not intend to include them. Agency has nothing to do with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: No. Anyone who gives his property to the Temple does not intend to include the clothing of his wife and children.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא knocks down רבי אבהו's proof by giving a different reason for the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו read the משנה as saying the clothes legally belong to the wife. רבי אבא says they may still belong to the husband. They are left alone only because his gift never included them. If so, the משנה proves nothing about agents.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives (consecrates) his property to the Temple
His intention, what he had in mind
Clothing

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said: No;
anyone who consecrates his property,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין דַּעְתּוֹ עַל כְּסוּת אִשְׁתּוֹ וּבָנָיו.
phrases.english: his intention is not on the clothing of his wife and his children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 10 by giving another reason for the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not necessarily רבי אבהו's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be explained by the giver's intention, so it does not show that the wife owns the items through agency.

steps.title: But תפילין are included even though he didn't think of them
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges רבי אבא. A person does not usually think of his תפילין when giving his property, yet a משנה says they are included. So lack of intention should not leave items out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא challenged it: Does a person have his תפילין in mind? Yet we learned: one who gives his property to the Temple, they value his תפילין and include them!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks רבי אבא's reason using a משנה about תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא's rule is that items the giver did not have in mind are not included. רבי זירא assumes no one thinks about his תפילין, yet the משנה includes them. That suggests intention is not what decides it.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it
תפילין
They value it for him (count it as part of what he gave)
We learned in a משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira challenged it:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם עַל תְּפִילָּיו?
phrases.english: And is a person's intention on his tefillin?
Yet we learned: one who consecrates his property,
they value his tefillin for him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבא's reason from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's claim that items the giver did not have in mind are left out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תפילין are presumably not in the giver's mind, yet a משנה includes them. So lack of intention does not exclude items.

steps.title: תפילין feel like a מצוה, but taking family clothes causes bad feelings
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that a person does have his תפילין in mind, because giving to the Temple feels like a מצוה. He does not want to include his family's clothes, because that would cause bad feelings at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Yes, a person does have his תפילין in mind. One who gives his property thinks: I am doing a מצוה. But a person does not have the clothes of his wife and children in mind, because of the bad feelings it would cause.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבי אבא by explaining why the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי accepts רבי אבא's rule that the giver's intention decides. He shows that intention fits both cases. A giver gladly includes his תפילין as part of the מצוה, but he would never take his family's clothes because it would cause fighting.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
I am doing a מצוה
Bad feelings, resentment

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: Yes;
a person's intention is on tefillin,
because one who consecrates his property thinks:
I am doing a מצוה.
But a person's intention is not
on the clothing of his wife and his children,
because of bad feelings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge in step 12 and keeps רבי אבא's reason standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the giver's intention differs for תפילין and for family clothes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No one thinks of his תפילין, so they should be left out just like the clothes.
steps.terutzMaskana: A giver does mean to include תפילין, since it feels like a מצוה. He does not mean to include his family's clothes, to avoid bad feelings.

steps.title: But the משנה also covers ערכין, where the Temple takes by force
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא begins a new challenge to רבי אבא. The משנה also talks about someone who owes an ערך, and from such a person the Temple takes items by force. The next step completes the challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא challenged it: But wasn't the case of those who owe ערכין also taught here? And we learned: those who owe ערכין, the Temple takes collateral from them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא opens a second challenge to רבי אבא. The גמרא is only setting it up here, and the full point comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא's reason depends on what the giver had in mind. The משנה from step 9 also covers someone who owes an ערך, and from such a person the Temple takes items by force. In that case his intention should not matter at all.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that
People who owe an ערך (a set value they promised the Temple)
They take collateral by force

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is not finished yet. רב אושעיא makes his full point in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya challenged it:
But weren't those obligated in valuations taught here?
phrases.notes: The משנה from step 9 mentions someone who gives his ערך, not only someone who gives his property.

phrases.english: And we learned: those obligated in valuations,
they take collateral from them;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רבי אבא's reason, after רבי זירא's challenge was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's reason that the giver's intention leaves the family's clothes out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: From someone who owes an ערך, the Temple takes items by force, so his intention should be irrelevant. Yet the משנה still leaves the family's clothes. Step 15 completes the argument.

steps.title: Nobody wants his things seized, yet they are seized
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא finishes his challenge. A person who owes an ערך does not want collateral taken from him, yet it is taken. So intention does not decide what is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a person really have in mind that his own things should be taken from him as collateral?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא finishes the challenge he started in step 14. A person who owes an ערך surely does not want his things taken, yet the Temple takes them anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא said the family's clothing is not included because the man never meant to include it. רב אושעיא shows that intention does not matter here: the person who owes an ערך does not want to lose his things, and they are still taken. So lack of intention cannot be the reason the clothes stay with the family.

keyTerms.meaning: his intention, what he has in mind
to take collateral from him
a fixed sum someone vows to give the Temple, based on a person's age and gender

phrases.english: And is a person's intention
upon himself, to have collateral taken from him?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם עַל עַצְמוֹ לְמַשְׁכְּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge רב אושעיא began in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's reason from step 11 that the clothes are excluded because the man does not intend to include them
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Seizing from a person who owes an ערך goes against his will, yet the Temple still takes the items. So intention cannot be what decides what goes to the Temple.

steps.title: New reason: the clothes count as already given to the family
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא drops the intention reason. He says that whoever gives his property to the Temple is treated as if he had given the clothing to his wife and children from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אבא said: anyone who gives his property to the Temple is treated like someone who gave his wife's and children's clothing to them from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא gives up his earlier reason and offers a new one. The family's clothing was never really his at the time he gave his property to the Temple, because it counts as already given to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old reason was "he didn't mean to include it." That fell apart in step 15. The new reason is about ownership: the clothing counts as belonging to the wife and children from the start, so there was nothing of his to give to the Temple. Agency still plays no part, so רבי אבהו's proof stays rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: one who gives all his property to the Temple
who transferred ownership
clothing
from the start, from the beginning

steps.confusionAlert: The word אֶלָּא means רבי אבא is dropping his first reason, the one about intention. He is not adding to it. He still agrees the clothes go to the family; only the reason has changed.
steps.whatToRemember: The family's clothing is not part of הקדש because it counts as already belonging to them, not because of agency and not because of the man's intention.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the long discussion that began with רבי אבהו's proof about agency. The dyed clothing case no longer proves anything about a שליח.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Abba said:
Anyone who consecrates his property
becomes like one who transferred to them
his wife's and children's clothing from the outset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אושעיא's challenge by replacing the reason it attacked
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the reasoning: from intention to ownership
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The clothes stay with the family because the man doesn't mean to include them
steps.terutzMaskana: The clothes stay with the family because they count as given to the family from the start, so they were never part of what he gave to the Temple

steps.title: A ברייתא about buying a field in someone else's name
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: someone who buys a field in another person's name cannot force that person to sell it. If he made a condition, he can force him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: if someone buys a field in another person's name, that person is not forced to sell it. But if he said "on condition," that person is forced to sell it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about buying with a third person involved. The wording is unclear, so the גמרא is setting up a question about what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two cases. In a plain purchase "in someone else's name," nobody can be forced to sell. If the buyer said "on condition," then the other person can be forced. Who is selling to whom is not clear yet, and the next steps explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: the Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
in the name of another person
we force, we compel
on condition

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who buys a field in the name of another
is not compelled to sell.
But if he said to him: "On condition"
he is compelled to sell.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן הַלּוֹקֵחַ שָׂדֶה בְּשֵׁם חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic that also involves buying with another person in the picture
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a field is bought in another's name, 'he' is not forced to sell; if the buyer said "on condition," 'he' is forced to sell. Who is forced, and to whom, is unclear; the גמרא asks this next.

steps.title: What does the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא is saying, because its wording is unclear.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means. This short question sets up רב ששת's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not clear who is being forced to sell, or why buying "in someone's name" would matter. The גמרא is not attacking the ברייתא. It only wants to understand the case.

keyTerms.meaning: what is it saying?

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an explanation of the ברייתא just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is buying, in whose name, and who is forced to sell

steps.title: רב ששת: the buyer used the name of the ריש גלותא
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the buyer bought the field using the name of the ריש גלותא. The ריש גלותא is not forced to "sell" it to him, unless the buyer made a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said, this is what it means: if someone buys a field from another person in the name of the ריש גלותא, the ריש גלותא is not forced to sell it to him. But if he said "on condition," the ריש גלותא is forced to sell it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת explains the case. A buyer buys a field but uses the name of the powerful ריש גלותא, and the question is whether the ריש גלותא must then pass the field to the real buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a powerful person's name keeps others from fighting over the sale. Without a condition, the ריש גלותא does not have to hand the field over officially (give the documents) to the real buyer. If the buyer set this up as a condition when he bought, the ריש גלותא can be forced to do it.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it means
the Exilarch, the head of the Jewish community in בבל
from another person

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב ששת, the person who might be forced to "sell" is the ריש גלותא, whose name was used, not the original seller.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said, this is what it is saying:
One who buys a field from another
in the name of the Exilarch

phrases.aramaic: אֵין כּוֹפִין אוֹתוֹ רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא לִמְכּוֹר.
phrases.english: that Exilarch is not compelled to sell.
phrases.notes: "Sell" here means officially passing the field to the real buyer, for example by giving him the documents.

phrases.english: But if he said "on condition"
the Exilarch is compelled to sell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 by explaining the case in the ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is about a buyer who used the name of the ריש גלותא. The ריש גלותא is forced to pass the field to the real buyer only if the buyer made a condition.

steps.title: Does the ברייתא clash with the view of the scholars of the West?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the רישא as רב ששת explained it. It infers that the buyer really does acquire the field. It then asks whether this argues with בני מערבא, who say a seller cannot transfer to someone he did not know about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: if someone buys a field in the name of the ריש גלותא, the ריש גלותא is not forced to 'sell' it to him. This shows that the buyer does acquire the field for himself. Shall we say this argues with בני מערבא? They say: who told the wheat seller that he was transferring the wheat to the householder?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא re-quotes the first part of the ברייתא as רב ששת explained it. It points out that this reading seems to clash with the view of the scholars of ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only says the ריש גלותא need not give the buyer papers. That implies the buyer already owns the field. But בני מערבא hold that if the seller thought he was selling to someone else, the real buyer does not acquire, because the seller never meant to give it to him.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master said": the גמרא re-quotes an earlier teaching so it can examine it
The Exilarch, the head of the Jews in בבל
"By implication": a conclusion drawn from what the text says
"Shall we say it argues with": the opening of a suggested contradiction
"People of the West": the scholars of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: The Master said:
One who buys a field in the name of the Exilarch –

phrases.aramaic: אֵין כּוֹפִין אוֹתוֹ רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא לִמְכּוֹר.
phrases.english: the Exilarch is not forced to sell it to him.
This implies that he does acquire it for himself;
phrases.notes: "He" is the real buyer. If the only issue is papers, the field must already be his.

phrases.english: shall we say this argues with the people of the West,
who say:
And who told the owner of the wheat
that he should transfer the wheat to the householder?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב ששת's explanation from Step 19 against another view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's reading of the רישא of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His reading implies that the buyer acquires the field. בני מערבא hold that a buyer cannot acquire when the seller thought he was selling to someone else.

steps.title: The buyer told the seller and the witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this is no problem. The case is one where the buyer told the field owner and the witnesses that he was really buying for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the problem is only this, it is not difficult. The case is where he told the field owner and told the witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא removes the contradiction by narrowing the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בני מערבא only object when the seller did not know who was really buying. Here the seller and the witnesses were told, so the seller knowingly transferred the field to the real buyer. The ריש גלותא's name was used only as cover.

keyTerms.meaning: "If it is because of this, it is no difficulty": a formula that brushes aside a challenge
"For example, where": introduces a narrowed case
Witnesses

phrases.english: If it is because of this – it is not difficult;
for example, where he told the owner of the field,
and told the witnesses.
phrases.notes: He told them that he was buying the field for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to let a buyer acquire even when the seller did not know about him, which goes against בני מערבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The seller and the witnesses knew the real buyer, so even בני מערבא agree that he acquires.

steps.title: Why should a condition bind the ריש גלותא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רב ששת's reading from the סיפא. If the buyer made a condition, the ריש גלותא is forced to sell. But the ריש גלותא can say he wants nothing to do with their deal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, look at the end part: if he said 'on condition,' the ריש גלותא is forced to sell. Why? Let the ריש גלותא say: I do not want your honor, and I do not want your disgrace!
steps.whatsHappening: Having saved the רישא, the גמרא now finds a real problem in the סיפא of רב ששת's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ריש גלותא never took part in the deal. A condition made between the buyer and the seller should not obligate him. He can say: "I want neither your honor nor your shame," meaning leave me out of it.

keyTerms.meaning: "Rather, say the end part": the challenge moves to the second half of the source
"On condition"
"Why?"

keyTerms.term: לָא יְקָרַיְיכוּ בָּעֵינָא וְלָא זִילוּתַיְיכוּ בָּעֵינָא
keyTerms.meaning: "I want neither your honor nor your disgrace": I am not involved in your affairs

steps.confusionAlert: Here "sell" does not mean a real sale. It means the ריש גלותא writes the buyer papers that confirm the field is his.

phrases.english: Rather, say the end part:
"on condition" –
the Exilarch is forced to sell.
Why?
Let the Exilarch say:
I do not want your honor,
and I do not want your disgrace!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רישא and challenges רב ששת's reading from the סיפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's reading of the סיפא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A condition made between other people cannot force the ריש גלותא, an outsider who never agreed to anything.

steps.title: אביי begins a new reading of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Because רב ששת's reading failed, אביי starts a new explanation of the ברייתא. It is about someone who buys a field in the name of his fellow, the ריש גלותא. His explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said, this is what it means: one who buys a field in the name of his friend, the ריש גלותא –
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins re-reading the ברייתא. His explanation continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי keeps the same case: a field bought in the name of 'his fellow, the ריש גלותא.' Here the word חבירו simply names that other person as the ריש גלותא. אביי is about to read the ruling differently, so that it does not force the ריש גלותא, who had no part in the deal. The rest of his explanation comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: "This is what it means": introduces a new reading of a source
His friend or fellow

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said,
this is what it is saying:
One who buys a field in the name of his friend,
the Exilarch –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב ששת's reading after the challenge in Step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת's reading treated the ריש גלותא as an outsider, so a condition could not bind him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'other person' (חבירו) in whose name the field was bought is the ריש גלותא. אביי's full explanation continues on the next amud.
